review: One of my favorite museum experiences worldwide! Bernard Tschumi’s masterpiece covers Athens historical layers by physically reconstructing them through five different levels. The context and the place in the city are omnipresent and shine through the building. The museum is generously laid out and there’s hardly any waiting times. The flows through the exhibits work smoothly and although there are huge numbers of visitors there is never any feeling of crowding. Full points for this jewel!

A great stop if you are exploring Athens. The building is modern with huge windows and a clear view of the Acropolis itself. Inside, you will find ancient sculptures, pottery, and a cool glass floor that shows ruins underneath. The top floor has the Parthenon pieces laid out like they were originally placed at scale, and the cafe has a solid view. Easy to enjoy even if you are not a history buff.

The Acropolis Museum initially feels expensive at 20 euros per adult admission but on leaving, we both felt it was justified. It was an incredibly wet day here in Athens and we needed an indoor venue. The museum is incredibly well laid with so much to see. There is a free cloakroom to leave bags and wet coats etc. Also underneath the museum is a vast excavation which can be visited or viewed through the glass floors (see photo). One tip is to take a pair of headphones with you to use with your phone for the audio tour (also free/included).  The museum have selected (I imagine with much difficulty and deliberation) about 60 items across the floors to tell you about. That takes at least 2 hours.  We spent a good afternoon here and I would have wanted to return as I felt that there was too much to see and take in.  Great views of the Parthenon (despite the weather!) and city from the upper floors.  Lots of staff on hand for advice and guidance. An excellent attraction - well done.

I visited the Acropolis Museum in Athens and the experience was absolutely incredible! The building's architecture is simply breathtaking and its beauty is fascinating. I loved that the museum is built directly on top of ruins, which are visible through the transparent floors, creating a unique connection to history. The collections are vast and beautifully presented, and the view from the top floor is breathtaking. What's more, tickets are free for young people under 25 from EU countries upon presentation of an ID card. It's an unmissable visit for history buffs.

I visited the Acropolis Museum today and it was an outstanding experience from start to finish. The building itself is stunning-modern, light-filled, and thoughtfully designed to let the ancient history shine. One of the highlights was walking over the glass floors and seeing the archaeological remains beneath your feet, which immediately grounds you in the depth of Athens' history.  The exhibits are beautifully curated and easy to follow, even without a guide. Seeing the original Caryatids up close was incredibly moving, and the Parthenon Gallery at the top-perfectly aligned with the Acropolis-was a real standout. The way the sculptures are displayed alongside clear explanations helps you truly understand their story and significance.  It's spacious, well-organised, and never felt overwhelming. I'd highly recommend visiting before or after the Acropolis itself-it adds so much context and appreciation. A must-see in Athens.

Pretty good museum. I think a audio tour could've been good. Is definitely maybe worth it.  Split across 3 levels the museum has tons of exhibits along with two videos going through the history. Some of the museum facilities need to be fixed but outside of that there's a lot to see. Would probably recommend going here just after seeing the acropolis.

Great experience I like how they built the museum on top of ruins, but have made it where you can see through the floor to see the ruins below the museum. Also, they’ve done a very nice job keeping the exhibit where they feel very close but keeping them still safe Building is a couple stories tall on the second story there is a Lego exhibit which I quite enjoyed and then the final floor has incredible views overlooking the city and the surrounding scenery overall, the experience was quite good. Staff was extremely friendly and kind. I was very happy to see the 6 sisters exhibit. Only five of them are there. The other one is in the British museum. If you visit the top of the hill, you will see they have Moved the real ones into the museum to keep them from getting Weather.

A stunning bridge between the ancient and modern world. A must-visit in Athens... The glass floors at the entrance let you look down into ancient excavations beneath your feet. The top floor is the showstopper. It’s arranged exactly like the Parthenon and offers a panoramic view of the actual temple on the hill. Seeing the original maidens up close is breathtaking. 🎟️ Tickets: Buy them online in advance to skip the long ticket booth lines. ☕ The Cafe: The restaurant terrace has one of the best views of the Acropolis in the city. Great for a frappe or lunch. 🕒 Timing: Go Friday evening if you can—it’s open late and usually less crowded. Essential. Do the Acropolis hike first, then come here to understand what you just saw.

Place contains obviously a rich amount of history on not only the architectural structures during that time, but also the condition and practices of the natives of Athens (Athenians). Like the name suggests, the goddess Athena had heavy influence and present with the ancient Athenians and that tribute is on display at the museum. I thought I had quite a bit of knowledge on the mythology of the Greeks but I learned a lot even about my favorite ones which are Athena and Artemis. They have an excavation site as well that you can visit which goes more into the traditions and practices that transpired over that long time period of Athenian existence which was interesting. Well worth a visit

Amazing place to read about Acropolis history. Recommend to visit the museum first before visit the ancient site. Also bring your own headphones, as there will be free guided tours.  For parents: Bring a small bag with a stroller. As big bags will have to be checked in for storage.
